o1.biggest_strength: It correctly brings back the paused front-of-pack winner, adds the missing taste hook from reviews, and gives launch-ready copy with counts.
o1.biggest_mistake: Two of the six primary texts are close variants of the same transparency idea, so the set is a little less varied than it could be.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the six angles fully distinct by separating office snack and price/value more clearly, while keeping the same sharp voice and launch plan.

o2.biggest_strength: It nails the real signals: relaunch the paused winner, test taste, address ₹90 head-on, and write in buyer language that sounds like The Whole Truth.
o2.biggest_mistake: It adds a testing setup and budget assumption that were not asked for, and a few claims like review quotes would still need the usual legal comfort check.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the excellent copy and launch order, but trim the media-testing assumptions or label them as optional so the deliverable stays purely copy-led.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 2 has more genuinely different angles and sharper brand voice, especially on price, 4 pm snacking, and gym texture. Output 1 is very good, but it doubles up more on the transparency idea.
